dish.title: Pan-Fried Pork and Cabbage Dumplings
dish.description: Ground pork and napa cabbage dumplings, pleated by hand and pan-fried to a crisp golden bottom with a short covered steam, served with a simple soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

recipe_version.title: Pan-Fried Pork and Cabbage Dumplings
recipe_version.description: Ground pork and napa cabbage dumplings, pleated by hand and pan-fried to a crisp golden bottom with a short covered steam, served with a simple soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: ground pork
ingredients.note: Plain ground pork (about 80/20), not lean tenderloin grind and not seasoned sausage. Not chops, tenderloin, or braised shoulder. Meat.

ingredients.name: napa cabbage
ingredients.note: about 3 packed cups once chopped (roughly 1/3 of a medium head)

ingredients.name: round dumpling wrappers
ingredients.note: HARD CONTRACT: store-bought round dumpling (jiaozi / gyoza-style) wrappers about 3 1/4 to 3 1/2 inches across, made from wheat flour and water (salt allowed). Egg-free: do not use yellow wonton or egg-roll wrappers. Buy a 12–16 oz pack with at least 32; keep extras wrapped. Wheat.
ingredients.preparation: kept covered with a damp towel while folding

ingredients.name: scallions
ingredients.note: divided: 3 for the filling (white and light-green parts plus some green), 1 green top thinly sliced for the dip
ingredients.preparation: finely minced (3) and thinly sliced (1 green top)

ingredients.name: soy sauce
ingredients.note: HARD CONTRACT: regular brewed soy sauce (soybeans + wheat). divided: 1 1/2 tbsp in the filling, 3 tbsp in the dipping sauce. Soy and wheat.

ingredients.name: toasted sesame oil
ingredients.note: divided: 2 tsp in the filling, 1 tsp in the dipping sauce. Sesame.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 1/2 tsp to draw water from the cabbage, 1/2 tsp in the filling

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.note: divided: 1 tsp in the filling, 2 tsp dusted on the tray so folded dumplings do not stick

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.note: canola or grapeseed; not peanut oil. divided: 1 1/2 tbsp per pan-fry batch

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: divided: 2 tbsp mixed into the filling, about 1/4 cup in a small bowl for sealing wrappers, 1/2 cup per batch for the covered steam (2 batches)

steps.title: Salt the cabbage, prep aromatics, and make the dip
steps.body: Toss the finely chopped napa cabbage with 1/2 tsp of the kosher salt in a bowl and let it stand 10 minutes to release water. Meanwhile, finely mince 3 of the scallions, thinly slice the green top of the fourth for the dip, grate the ginger, and mince the garlic. Stir together the dipping sauce in a small bowl: 3 tbsp of the soy sauce, the 3 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar, 1 tsp of the toasted sesame oil, and the sliced scallion green. Gather the cabbage in a clean kitchen towel by handfuls and squeeze hard until no more liquid runs out; discard the liquid. About 10 minutes.

steps.title: Mix the pork filling
steps.body: In a large bowl combine the ground pork, squeezed cabbage, minced scallions, ginger, garlic, the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp soy sauce, the remaining 2 tsp toasted sesame oil, sugar, white pepper, the remaining 1/2 tsp kosher salt, 1 tsp of the cornstarch, and 2 tbsp of the water. Stir firmly in one direction with chopsticks or a spatula for about 1 minute until the filling turns sticky and holds together. About 4 minutes.

steps.title: Fill and pleat the dumplings
steps.body: Dust a sheet pan with the remaining 2 tsp cornstarch. Pour about 1/4 cup of the water into a small bowl. Keep the wrappers under a damp towel. Hold a wrapper in your palm, place a level 1 tbsp of filling in the center, and wet the outer edge halfway around with a fingertip of water. Fold into a half-moon, pinch the top center closed, then make 3 or 4 small pleats on the front edge on each side, pressing each pleat against the flat back edge to seal. Set the dumpling on the tray seam up so it sits on a flat bottom. Repeat to make 32 dumplings, keeping finished ones covered. Honest home-cook folding pace is about 45 seconds each, so allow about 25 minutes. About 25 minutes.

steps.title: Pan-fry and steam the first batch
steps.body: Heat 1 1/2 tbsp of the neutral oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet with a tight lid over medium-high heat for about 1 minute. Arrange 16 dumplings flat-side down in snug rings, just touching. Fry undisturbed until the bottoms are golden, about 2 minutes. Carefully pour in 1/2 cup of the water (it will sputter), cover immediately, and lower the heat to medium. Steam 7 minutes, until the wrappers turn translucent and the filling is firm and cooked through (160 F if checked). Uncover and cook about 2 minutes more until the water is gone and the bottoms re-crisp and release. Slide onto a platter crisp-side up. About 12 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the second batch
steps.body: Wipe the skillet if any bits scorched. Repeat with the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp neutral oil, the remaining 16 dumplings, and the remaining 1/2 cup water: 1 minute preheat, 2 minutes fry, 7 minutes covered steam, 2 minutes uncovered re-crisp. About 12 minutes.

steps.title: Serve with the soy-vinegar dip
steps.body: Serve the dumplings crisp-side up with the soy-vinegar dipping sauce on the side. Not deep-fried. Not boiled. No shrimp, no chicken. kitchen_tested is false.

components.name: round dumpling wrappers
components.contract: Store-bought wheat-and-water round dumpling wrappers; egg-free (no yellow wonton/egg-roll wrappers).

equipment: 12-inch nonstick skillet with a tight-fitting lid
clean kitchen towel for squeezing cabbage
recipe_version.time_clock: Prep 39 = 10 salt cabbage / aromatics / dip / squeeze + 4 mix filling + 25 fold 32 dumplings (about 45 seconds each). Cook 24 = two pan-fry batches of 12 (1 preheat + 2 fry + 7 covered steam + 2 uncovered re-crisp). Total 63. The 30–45 band in selection was rough; this clock includes honest fold time.
recipe_version.heat: Medium-high to preheat the oil and fry the bottoms; medium for the covered steam; medium uncovered to evaporate water and re-crisp. Stovetop only. No deep-fry, no boil, no oven.
recipe_version.doneness: Bottoms deep golden and crisp; tops tender and translucent, not gummy-white. Filling firm, juicy, no pink, 160 F if checked. Water fully evaporated before plating so bottoms stay crisp. kitchen_tested is false.

dietary_eligibility.nut_policy_note: No peanuts, tree nuts, or cashews. Sesame is an allergen token (toasted sesame oil), not a tree nut. Frying oil is contracted as canola or grapeseed, not peanut oil.
dietary_eligibility.hh001_reason: Ground pork is meat other than fish. HH001 does not eat pork. The filling and dip are dairy-free, but that does not make the meal HH001-eligible.

recipe_version.dietary_label_note: Unconditional dairy_free. No milk, butter, cheese, cream, or yogurt anywhere; wrappers are wheat and water. Pork is present, so not vegetarian or plant-based.

coverage_contribution: Opens the dumpling format (0 in the base). Deepens chinese-inspired beyond ginger-scallion fish packets. Ground pork is a new pork shape (live pork is cider braise, jerk chops, and air-fryer tenderloin). Adds the crisp-bottom pan-fry + steam technique — a texture story the catalog lacks.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with Ginger Scallion Fish Packets: shares chinese-inspired ginger/scallion aromatics, but steamed fish in parchment vs. pleated pork dumplings pan-fried then steamed. Compared with Jamaican Jerk Pork Chops / Air-Fryer Honey-Mustard Pork Tenderloin / Cider-Braised Pork Shoulder: same animal, but ground pork in wrappers vs. chops, tenderloin, and braise. Compared with Spiced Lamb Meatballs: ground-meat shaping, but lamb in Mediterranean tomato sauce. Compared with Peanut Noodle Stir-Fry / Sesame Soba Noodle Bowl: soy-sesame flavors, but noodles and plant protein. Deliberately not chicken potstickers (chicken load), not shrimp dumplings (shellfish), not a stir-fry.
